title: Refraction of light (আলোর প্রতিসরণ)
placement: Book page 243, topic 9.1 আলোর প্রতিসরণ, with চিত্র ৯.০১–৯.০২ and টেবিল ৯.০১; it carries the laws of refraction (9.1.1, চিত্র ৯.০৪–৯.০৫, pp. 244–247, but not the coin নিজে করো: that is coin-in-cup) and the relative refractive index (9.1.2, pp. 247–248).
description: Refraction of light (pages 243–248, topics 9.1, 9.1.1 and 9.1.2). A thick block of clear glass on a plain sand-coloured table against a calm deep-blue backdrop, and a small torch riding a graduated aluminium arc whose centre is the point of incidence, so it always shines there; the student turns it (drag or arrow keys) to set θ₁ from 0° to 80°. Five steps, one tap each, slow: (1) the light goes in, bends and slows: wavefronts march, closer together in the glass, and the panel shows the book's উদাহরণ (v = c/n for table ৯.০১) and n = c/v; (2) the normal (লম্ব) and the angles θ₁, θ₂: into a denser medium the ray bends toward the normal (a θ₂–θ₁ graph); (3) the first law in true 3D: the upright plane through the incident ray and the normal stands at 90° to the surface, and the camera swings round to look along it, where the incident ray, the normal and the refracted ray fall on one line; (4) the second law: Measure at three angles leaves dots on a sin θ₁–sin θ₂ graph, a straight line of steepness n₂ (n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂); the medium can be water, glass or diamond, and earlier lines stay faint; (5) water poured over a glass slab: from water into glass sin θ₁ / sin θ₂ = 1.14, the refractive index of glass with respect to water (0.88 the other way). Rays traced exactly with Snell's law at each boundary; a faint reflected ray whose strength follows Fresnel. Test: five questions (speed in water, the first law, the book's two উদাহরণ, the relative index), every wrong choice with its own note. Phone-first, Bangla and English.
